text:
sasha: quick idea — should the console ask for explicit tenant consent when granting cross-tenant roles to a service account? thinking about enterprise audits + auto-routing policies.
jorge: depends — are we talking interactive grant (admin clicks) or api-based onboarding?
sasha: both. interactive is where UX matters (microcopy, fallback), but API flows need clear telemetry and an optional approval webhook.
mike: flagging an existing constraint: dedicated routing policies can create implicit scope expansion. if a tenant assigns a route that touches multiple clusters, the effective permission set increases. we should surface that.
sasha: exactly. example: assigning `route:all` plus `model:deploy` ends up enabling cross-region inference. want a quick surface that says "this grant enables routing to X (dedicated/pool)".
anna: +1 to explicit surface. also legal asked for a one-click audit note that snapshots the grant reason and the selected routing policies. could be a modal step.
jorge: tradeoff: too many modals will slow power users. maybe an inline banner with an optional expand -> "show expanded effects" and a checkbox if admin wants a recorded justification.
mike: for API flows we can add a header `X-Grant-Justification` and if present we persist it in the audit log; otherwise we generate a system note saying "no justification provided".
audit-bot: NOTE: when granted_scopes includes `routing:modify` or `deploy:all` an audit entry will be created automatically. See https://internal.example.com/audit/guide
sasha: on telemetry, we should tag grants that touch quotas (e.g., route qps > 0) so billing/quota dashboards can correlate role changes with sudden spikes.
anna: and for rollouts: canary role grants? like grant to a subgroup for 48h then auto-rollout if no errors. would help avoid mass misconfigurations.
mike: implementable: attach `rollout_policy: {type: canary, window: 48h, check: error_rate<0.5%}` to the grant payload. backend will atomically provision and revert if checks fail.
jorge: UI needs to show expected fallout (what routes/tokens will be valid) and provide a revert button. wireframe idea: compact diff view with affected routes + quota deltas.
sasha: microcopy request: avoid jargon. don't show raw scope strings by default. map `routing:modify` -> "Modify routing policies (may enable cross-tenant routing)" with a learn more link.
anna: example text suggestion: "This grant lets the principal change which inference pools routes use. This may increase cross-region traffic and affect quotas." short and neutral.
jorge: security question: do we allow delegation (admin A grants admin B ability to grant)? if yes, we must show chain-of-trust in the audit UI.
mike: agree. show 3 layers: granter, delegate flag, and active approver if approval flow used. store all in `grant_metadata`.
sasha: any objections to adding an opt-in "consent banner" for high-impact grants that persists on the principal's profile? admins can opt out org-wide.
anna: org-wide opt-out needs org-admin permission. legal will want retention TTL for consent notes (e.g., 7 years).
jorge: implementation note: we should keep the server-side enforcement simple: the console sends a `grant_preview` API call which returns `effective_permissions`, `affected_routes`, `quota_impacts`, `audit_recommendation` that the UI renders. final `grant` call includes optional `justification` and `rollout_policy`.
sasha: here's a quick proto for the preview response:
```
{
  "effective_permissions": ["model:deploy","route:modify"],
  "affected_routes": ["tenant-a/route-1","shared-pool/global"],
  "quota_impacts": {"qps_delta": 200, "tokens_month": 1_000_000},
  "high_impact": true
}
```
jorge: looks good. small ask: include `can_revoke_by` list and `revert_endpoint` if canary is enabled.
mike: also include `telemetry_tags` for the grant so metrics platform can attach time-series to the change. e.g., `grant:service-account:payment-batch-job`.
audit-bot: REMINDER: retention policy for audit entries in staging is 90 days; for prod legal retention mark is 7 years.
sasha: ok next steps: eng-platform to spec `grant_preview` + `grant` payload by next Tues. design to mockup inline banner + compact diff. product to draft microcopy (anna). security to confirm delegation model (jorge). I'll spin up a short RFC thread after this. :thumbsup:
mike: i'll draft the backend schema and list of telemetry tags.
anna: I'll put some microcopy options in figma by EOD Fri.
jorge: security will validate the chain-of-trust model and retention implications.
sasha: thanks all — this helps. feel free to drop quick comments in the RFC when it's up.
